filesChanged: packages/pi-envoy/extensions/askgate/askgate-core.ts — askIdentity keys a block ask on its id as well as its opening; Breaker.revised deduplicates at its own boundary.
packages/pi-envoy/extensions/askgate/askgate.test.ts — four regressions: the reviewer's case through both callers, the no-id opening key, the dedupe alone and the id key alone.
packages/pi-envoy/README.md — the list bound says what the code does.
trickyParts: The reviewer's recipe for making the de-duplication read fail does not work as written: two uploads of one name give one document at version 2, because the server matches an upload to an existing artifact of that exact name, and an upload of that name under another content type is refused. The ambiguity is reached instead through artifactByReference's other branch — a second document whose name is the first document's slug — which is what this round's live run used.
The id key had to leave two unidentified asks that open alike as one thing, or an agent rewording only an ask's tail would loop for ever; the key is the id and the opening, never the id alone.
deviations: The round-3 fixture dispatch://INFRA-365 was closed after the tester released it, so this round's live run uses a new unassigned fixture, dispatch://INFRA-373.
No simplify pass: one per pull request, run in the first implementing round.
openQuestions: sjawhar/legion#2159 is still open and this branch carries its commits; the architect watches it and the plan's "when #2159 merges" step runs before the review round that approves the head.
discoveredComplexity: Every finding of rounds 1 to 3 has been one fault: something quietly deciding an ask is not judged while the record still reads as judged and clean. This round's was multiplicity — one refusal counted twice because two asks collapsed to one key — and the remedy that closes it, keying a block on its id, is also what the reviewer had filed as a separate minor.

A path whose whole purpose is to leave a trace when nobody judged an ask could not be left on a unit case, and reaching it live took a correction to how Dispatch stores a re-uploaded document. That correction is itself worth keeping: an upload of an existing name versions that document and never makes a second one.
